prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Sign in with existing pet profile or create a new desktop account"]
1: ["Choose Visual Render Style", "Select your preferred art style before generating your desktop companion.", "3D Stylized, Pixel Art, Hand-Drawn Anime"]
2: ["Generating desktop pet animations and sound profiles..."]
3: ["Confirm Desktop Pet Rendering", "Check that your companion appears on your screen and your system tray menu is active.", "Pet rendered on screen; Tray controls accessible; Interaction active"]
4: []
5: ["Path setup takes under 2 minutes. You can customize companion traits anytime later."]
6: ["Upload Clear, Front-Facing Photos", "For accurate 3D desktop pet rendering, use well-lit photos showing your pet facing the camera directly."]
7: ["Desktop Pet Controls Checklist", "Quickly review how to interact with your pet on your desktop toolbar and screen."]
8: ["Play ready chime when done"]
9: ["Sign in with your primary account to preserve your desktop pet species, items, and companion memory."]
